chapter.title: Interrupts
chapter.para: A guest gets the interrupts of the devices that the hypervisor emulates for it; the hypervisor does not pass the interrupts of the host to a guest, except as this chapter says.

section.title: SRQ_HV_INT_001
section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall emulate for each VM a pair of 8259A interrupt controllers, programmed by the guest through their ports (initialization and operation command words, interrupt masks, priorities, end of interrupt, cascade through IRQ 2, reading of the request and service registers), and shall reset it with the VM.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for x86_64 drives the 8259A pair.

section.title: SRQ_HV_INT_002
section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall deliver an interrupt of the emulated controller to the guest when the guest can take it, that is when its interrupt flag is set and it is not in the shadow of an instruction, and shall let a guest that has halted with interrupts enabled wait for one.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: An interrupt must not interrupt what the guest does not allow.

section.title: SRQ_HV_INT_003
section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall emulate for each VM the distributor of a GICv2 for the interrupts 0 to 31 and one CPU, and shall give the guest the CPU interface of the host through the virtual CPU interface of the processor.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for arm64 drives a GICv2, and needs the interrupt of its timer.

section.title: SRQ_HV_INT_004
section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall give the guest the interrupt of its virtual timer when the guest's distributor is on and the interrupt is enabled in it, with the priority that the guest gave it, shall take it back if the guest disables it before it was taken, and shall deliver each interrupt of the timer once.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The guest must see the tick as its own, once.

section.title: SRQ_HV_INT_005
section.para: The hypervisor shall use, for itself, only the interrupts of the host that it needs: on x86_64 the local APIC timer, on arm64 the virtual timer and the maintenance interrupt of the GIC; it shall ignore a spurious interrupt, report any other interrupt on its console and go on, and treat an exception of its own as a fatal error.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The hypervisor must not be disturbed by what it did not ask for.
